Ancient Isle
Ancient Isle is located in the far east of the map. You can spot it between Snowcap Island and Mushgrove Swamp. Be careful when sailing here, because whirlpools around the island can sink your boat.
Once you land, you can buy the Stone Rod for 3,000C$ and the Phoenix Rod for 40,000C$. This place is well known for the Ancient Archives, where you can craft rods in Fisch after collecting all the required materials.
Aquarium
The Aquarium is your own personal hub, which you can access from the Aquariums menu. Here you can place up to 10 of your fish to earn passive income and XP every hour.
Make sure to claim your rewards from the menu before you go offline so they don’t go to waste. You can also visit other players’ aquariums and see their collections.
Atlantis
Atlantis is a huge underwater city that you can only explore if you have the correct diving gear. You can enter it through the Grand Reef.
Inside, you will find a merchant, an inn keeper, and several trial pools like the Poseidon, Kraken, and Ethereal Abyss pools. It is a great place to complete your bestiary, but the risk is high.
Boreal Pines
Boreal Pines is a snowy island that you can only reach through a portal in the Southern Ocean. Once you are here, head to Boreal Hollow to take on the Goliath Siphonophore Hunt.
You can also explore the Crystal Fissure to find the Fisch Frostwyrm Hunt. If you have a Stellar Lens, you can use it to summon Lyren for the Celestial Congregation.
Castaway Cliffs
Castaway Cliffs is a quiet cliff-side island with its own fish pool. You can buy the Firefly rod for 9,500C$ and the Rainbow Cluster Rod for 250,000C$ from here, but it only spawns during the rainbow event. The place has 4-5 NPCs with simple quests.
Cursed Isle
Cursed Isle is a spooky island location in Fisch that only spawns during the foggy spring/autumn nights. You can spot it near the north of Snowcap Island, and it has a Cthulhu statue at the center.
There are no sub-locations to explore, but you can buy the Great Dreamer Rod in Fisch for 275,000C$ and the Great Dream Waker harpoon for 1,500,000C$.
Desolate Deep
Desolate Deep is a dark underwater area, and to go deeper, you will need advanced diving gear. The good thing is that you can buy it here for 15,000C$.
You need diving gear in Fisch to enter. Inside, you can visit the Desolate Pocket, the Luminescent Cavern, and the Crimson Cavern, which have dragon hunts.
The Brine Pool is the most dangerous spot because it is full of acid; if you fall in it, you will die. You can buy the Trident Striker, one of the best harpoon guns in Fisch, from here for 175,000C$.
Drylands
The Drylands is a big desert area in the Fisch map. The dust storms drain your health, but they also give you double luck.
Here you can sift through the sand to find treasure using a marrow rod with a sand sifter or a rod with the Dune enchantment. Be careful; there is a huge scorpion that roams around called the Terrosunder. If you get too close, it can instantly kill you.
Everturn Forest
Everturn Forest is a forest island located in the north of Mushgrove Swamp. It has a unique mechanism that changes the island’s appearance according to the seasons.
During winter, the ponds will freeze; during spring, the flowers will spread around the island; and during autumn, the leaves will spread around the island. This is the place where you can catch the Oakling fish.
Forsaken Shores
Forsaken Shores is a rocky island with two main fishing spots, the shore and the pond. Each spot has its own fish, so try both if you want to fill your bestiary. It is a good island to visit once you have left the starter area.
Grand Reef
Grand Reef is filled with colorful reefs, and its main job is to lead you to Atlantis, so many players pass through here on the way. You can also visit the Atlantean Storm and Mermaid Cove to complete your bestiary.
Lost Jungle
Lost Jungle is a thick jungle island northeast of Sunstone Island. This is the place where people hunt for Mossjaw in Fisch.
You need to find five runes and unlock the Forgotten Temple to access the hunt area. You can also visit the Living Garden, the Toxic Grove, and the Nectar Den. Make sure to buy a gas mask before entering the Toxic Grove, or you will take damage.
Mariana’s Veil
Mariana’s Veil is a deep-sea region that you can only explore if you have a submarine. It has many sub-locations, such as Volcanic Vents, Challenger’s Deep, and the Calm Zone.
The deepest part is the Obsidian Trench, where you can start the Skolopendra hunt. Completing its full bestiary will unlock the Chasm-Stalker rod.
Moosewood
Moosewood is the starter island where you first spawn in Fisch. You can find a merchant, an appraiser, an inn keeper, and a shipwright here.
Here you can set your spawn point and buy your first Fisch boat. You can also unlock a hidden market called the Shady Bazaar after completing Todd’s quest.
Mushgrove Swamp
A dark, mushroom-filled swamp with glowing plants and murky water. You can buy mushroom potions, poison gear, and the Marsh Rod from swamp NPCs. A hole near the marsh leads to the Carrot Garden. There you can fish for unique catches or buy the carrot rod for 75,000 coins.
Northern Expedition
The Northern Expedition is a cold and risky mountain route in the far north. It has many stops, including Northern Summit, Frigid Cavern, Cryogenic Canal, and Glacial Grotto.
Each place has its own fish, and the fishing gets harder as you go higher. You can buy oxygen tanks, a winter cloak, and an advanced glider from here.
Ocean
The ocean is the big open water that connects every island. It is also the main spot for global events like Megalodon Hunts, Whirlpools, and Sunken Chest drops. There are small stops, including Harvester’s Spike, Haddock Rock, and Birch Cay. Birch Cay has a hidden hatch that leads to an underground bunker.
Roslit Bay
Roslit Bay is an early island with an active volcano, a town pond, and a boat dock. It is a good second stop after Moosewood. You can buy the Magma Rod, a glider, a Meteor totem, and Crab Cages from here. You can also visit Roslit Pond and the Roslit Volcano to reel in rare fish and make money fast in Fisch.
Scoria Reach
Scoria Reach is another volcanic island with flowing lava. Here you can explore inside the volcano, but you need to have Scoria Armor equipped, or you will take damage. Once inside, you can buy the Igneous Rupturer rod for 5,000,000C$.
Snowcap Island
Snowcap Island is a snowy island located to the southeast of Moosewood Island. It has a pond, a cave, and a hidden spot called Snowburrow. To open Snowburrow, click three cracks in 10 seconds, and the door closes after 30 seconds. Here you can buy the Windset Totem for 2,000 C$ and the Blue Moon Totem for 120,000C$.
Statue of Sovereignty
The Statue of Sovereignty is a famous landmark and a key place for upgrades. Inside, you will find a Keeper’s Altar where you can use different relics to enchant your rod in Fisch.
Sunstone Island
Sunstone Island is a calm island in the middle of the map. It has shops, NPCs, and a steady fish pool.
Explore the Fisch Mineshaft, where you break rubble and use a minecart puzzle to get a Rough Geode and a Cut Gem that unlocks the Shard of Time. This is used to craft Merlin’s Staff Rod. You can also buy the sundial totem for 2,000C$ from here.
Terrapin Island
Terrapin Island is located southwest of Moosewood Island. You can come here to buy a fish radar, one of the most important pieces of equipment that tells you the abundance of the fish in an area.
You can explore the cave during foggy nights and use the Turtle keystone to unlock Luminescent Cavern to find the entrance to the secret Cultist Lair.
The Deep
The Deep is an underwater city located at the far north of the map. There are 3 primary sub-locations you can explore: Outer Deep, Lower Deep, and the Gloomy Crevice, and hunt the Monstrous Cusk. You can also talk to Dr. Monty in his lab to unlock the Halibut Harpoon in Fisch.
Tidefall
Tidefall is another huge underwater cave system located under the ocean. You enter it through an opening under the ocean, but the pressure might kill you, so make sure to take an Abyssal Tonic before you try to enter Tidefall. Once inside, you can explore Tidefall Castle, Coral Bastion, and Sunken Reliquary.
Trade Plaza
Trade Plaza is a hub where players can trade fish with each other. You need to be at least level 25 or higher to enter this area. Speak to the Trade Plaza Traveler at the south of Moosewood docks to enter this zone.
Treasure Island
Treasure Island is a treasure-themed island with golden hills that are surrounded by shimmering water. Here you can complete quests and buy the treasure rod for 50,000C$. Completing its bestiary will give you a treasure chest bobber as a reward.
Vertigo
Vertigo is a special area that you can reach through a Strange Whirlpool. It has four main sublocations you can explore: Vertigo Caves, Vertigos Dip, The Depths, and Aether. To unlock the depths, you must find the depths key and open the door. This is the place where you get the Rod Of The Depths. You can also complete the Keeper’s puzzle to access the secret Aether zone and fish in the void.
Wrath of Olympus
Wrath of Olympus is located under Atlantis. It has six layers, and each layer has its own puzzles, fish, rods, and boss challenges.
Every layer is based on Gods from Greek mythology: Bellona’s Frenzy of War, Apollo’s Song of Light (unlocks Apollo’s Sunshot Rod), Poseidon’s Storm of Floods, Zeus’ Thunder of Chaos, Hades’ Underworld of Indefinite, and Olympian Fissure. You need to solve puzzles to enter each zone layer by layer.
This sums up our guide on all the locations in Fisch map. Make sure to catch all the fish and complete every location’s bestiary.
Where do you spawn in Fisch?
When you first launch Fisch, you spawn in Moosewood. Here, you can catch your first fish and begin progressing through the game.
How do you reach Vertigo in Fisch?
Jump into the Strange Whirlpool with a beam of light shooting straight up into the sky.

(Bloomberg) -- Iran received a letter sent by US Vice President JD Vance to its top security official, the semi-official Tasnim news agency reported, with one of the country’s top negotiators later suggesting Tehran’s positions on ending the war will not be compromised. 
Tasnim didn’t disclose the contents of the letter addressed to Mohsen Rezaee, the hardline chief of the Supreme National Security Council, or say whether Tehran is preparing a reply. 
But in a post on X after the letter was reportedly received, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, one of Iran’s negotiators in previous talks to end the war, wrote that “Iran’s conditions have been repeatedly and clearly stated to the mediators.” 
“The carrot-and-stick approach has no effect on Iran,” Ghalibaf continued without mentioning Vance’s letter or saying if his comments constituted a formal reply.    
The highly unusual approach by Vance comes as President Donald Trump repeatedly threatens to resume airstrikes on Iran amid an impasse in negotiations to end the eight-month war. Trump told reporters on Wednesday he authorized Vance to contact Tehran, saying the letter was meant to assist Iran with “medical supplies and various things,” without providing specifics.
The Wall Street Journal earlier reported that Vance had written to Rezaee in a bid to revive peace negotiations. 
The development follows high-level talks in Tehran this week with officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan. The parties described the meeting as positive and agreed to continue discussions, though no formal second round has been set. 
Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei reiterated earlier this week that his country has certain conditions that must be met before an end to the war can be agreed. At the heart of the impasse is Tehran’s ongoing attacks on ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, while the US has imposed a naval blockade on Iran’s ports. 
Iran has repeatedly said in recent weeks that it remains open to diplomacy, with Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi writing on X on Thursday that while “our Brave Armed Forces are fully prepared to defend the Homeland, Iran continues to give diplomacy a chance to succeed.”
The US and Israel started bombing Iran in late February, triggering retaliatory strikes by Tehran on Gulf nations hosting US military bases. The war has killed thousands — mostly Iranian civilians — while disrupting energy shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and roiling global markets.

Alexander Zverev ensured he would overtake Jannik Sinner in the rankings and become world number one for the first time next week with a 6-4, 7-5 victory over Tallon Griekspoor in the last 16 of the Vienna Open on Thursday.
The 29-year-old, who has enjoyed a stellar season capped by titles at the French and US Opens, will become Germany’s second men’s number one after Boris Becker in 1991 when the new rankings are published on Monday.
Zverev’s victory, which was sealed with an ace, was followed by a ceremony on court when he was joined by his team and Thomas Muster, the only Austrian to have topped the rankings, to mark the feat.
“[It is] very special. To have the feeling to be on the top of the world is amazing,” said Zverev, who will be the 30th man to top the rankings since they were introduced in 1973.
“It’s different than winning a tournament, winning a title, but it’s such a special feeling to know that the number one is going to be next to your name when the new rankings come out,” he added.

Zverev would be the first to admit that injuries to Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz, who between them won every Grand Slam title in the 2024 and 2025 seasons, had eased his ascent to the top of the rankings.
Sinner decided to end his season in early October to recover from a knee injury, but world number three Alcaraz was in action in Vienna earlier on Thursday and saved four set points to beat Nikoloz Basilashvili 6-1 7-6(11).
Zverev came close to taking the number one ranking in 2022 at the French Open but tore ankle ligaments in his semifinal against Rafa Nadal and missed the rest of the season.
“I had to wait, but sometimes you’ve got to wait for the best things in life. So it is how it is. I’m super happy, super thrilled,” he said, adding, “This year, I mean, I have no words for this year. Again, I’m just thankful. I’m happy and all of the above.”

Humanitarian aid set to enter Oleshky as a rare Russia-Ukraine truce holds for a third day
A Ukrainian official says that humanitarian aid is set to arrive in the stricken Russian-occupied city of Oleshky on Friday, as a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine stretches into its third day

Humanitarian aid is poised to roll into the stricken city of Oleshky on Friday, a Ukrainian official said, as a localized ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine stretched into a third day and military units cleared away landmines.
Moscow and Kyiv have observed the truce in and around the devastated southern Ukrainian city since Tuesday, despite remaining locked in war since Russia’s all-out invasion of its neighbor more than 4 ½ years ago. Previous efforts to secure ceasefires either never worked out or the truces quickly fell apart.
The planned six-day ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky has also brought a rare and welcome stillness for civilians in the nearby city of Kherson, which is held by Ukraine and has also been wracked by the war.
Elsewhere, Russia’s Defense Ministry said air defenses downed 1,214 Ukrainian drones overnight in one of the largest drone attacks launched by Kyiv. Around half of the drones were heading to the Russian capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said.
Ukraine said Russia fired 112 drones at seven locations across the country.
The Oleshky ceasefire has held for 54 hours, officials say
Both sides thanked U.S. first lady Melania Trump for what the White House said was her role in helping broker the temporary ceasefire so that food and medical supplies can reach some desperate 2,000 people trapped in Oleshky. Pope Leo XIV also pressed for a truce.
“The ceasefire has been in place for 54 hours now,” Ukrainian ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said Thursday, adding that aid deliveries were due to begin the following day. “The parties are fully adhering to the agreements, and no violations of the ceasefire have been reported.”
His Russian counterpart, Yana Lantratova, confirmed the truce was holding and that Russian engineers are working on de-mining Oleshky roads.
“Both sides are fully honoring their commitments, and no violations have been recorded,” she said. “This allows military personnel to continue clearing roads of mines and to prepare a safe passage for the humanitarian convoy.”
Local people will also be able to evacuate, either into Russia or Ukraine, officials say. The mechanics of how that might work were unclear.
Russian leader Putin says Elon Musk is ‘a genius’
Moscow and Kyiv are keen to curry favor with Washington ahead of possible three-way talks next month between Russia, Ukraine and the United States.
American military support is vital for Ukraine, but U.S. President Donald Trump has recently indicated that he is disengaging with Kyiv as he waived sanctions on Russia and publicly chided Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
Tankers carrying Russian diesel are currently sailing to the United States, and Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov will travel to the U.S. for a G20 ministerial meeting in Atlanta, Georgia, starting Friday, according to Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova.
European leaders, on the other hand, have been trying to diplomatically isolate Russian President Vladimir Putin over Moscow’s invasion and what they call a campaign of sabotage across the continent.
Ukraine earlier this month reported sudden and unexpected limits on Starshield, the military-grade version of the Starlink satellite internet service owned by Elon Musk’s SpaceX that is the backbone of Ukraine’s drone operations and communications.
Putin said that Russia has been in contact with the American tech titan to coordinate their orbiting activities because it is building its own equivalent of Starlink.
“Elon Musk is a genius. Truly, a real genius,” Putin said late Wednesday.
“We and our American partners value this relationship, and despite all the political issues, we continue to work closely together,” he added.

Audio reveals exchanges between control centre and drivers before deadly Spain train crash
- Published
Audio recordings published in Spanish media reveal conversations between train drivers and a railway control centre in the minutes leading up to a deadly train crash that killed at least 68 people and injured dozens.
Officials are investigating the cause of the disaster, which occurred when a train travelling from Madrid to Seville barrelled into a stationary train on Wednesday morning.
Three audio recordings between the control centre in Madrid and two train drivers appear to show that one high-speed train was given clearance to move even though another some 25km (15 miles) up ahead had stalled.
The release of the recordings comes as Spain begins three days of national mourning for one of the worst rail disasters in Europe's modern history.
One train, run by state-owned operator Renfe, had 397 passengers on board. Ahead of it on the same line was a train run by private operator Iryo, with 147 passengers.
A reported issue with the automatic signalling system - a computer failure - had forced all trains to halt on the affected stretch.
But later the Renfe train was ordered to proceed in "error", according to Spain's transport minister.
Audio recordings published by Spanish news outlets including El Pais and RTVE reveal the conversations that took place between the two train's drivers and the control centre in the Spanish capital ahead of the crash.
In one recording, a control centre operator tells the Renfe driver to resume its journey at normal speed after some technical issues.
"Continue your journey and then proceed under [Lateral Signalling Block], at normal speed with normal operation," the control centre operator says to the driver.
The driver replies, "At normal speed?" To which the controller says: "Yes."
The Lateral Signaling Block is a back-up or alternative train system used when the automatic signalling or data transmission system fails.
Later, the driver of the other Iryo train says in another audio recording that communication with the train-control system has been lost and they are stationary at Urda.
The train "is stationary in front of the entry signal at Urda", the driver tells the control centre operator. After a series of exchanges, the driver is then told to "resume the journey" normally.
The Iryo driver then contacts the control centre again, according to a later recording, saying they cannot start the train. "The train won't allow me to control the [security] system. That's why I am still stopped in front of the entry signal," they say.
The latter recording suggests that the controller had been notified that the Iryo train remained stationary as the Renfe train approached.
Iryo said its train, which had 147 passengers on board, was "struck from behind" by another train, by Renfe train which was carrying 397 passengers.
Spain's transport minister Óscar Puente said on Wednesday that the decision to instruct the trains to move again, without any speed restrictions, was "inexplicable".
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said the "whole of Spain is grieving", adding that "lives have been shattered, families have been torn apart, the pain is immense".
Emergency crews worked through the night under powerful floodlights to cut open metal carriages in the search for victims, with many of those killed in the crash still to be identified.
Hundreds of personnel have been deployed to the disaster site to assist with recovery efforts, according to Spain's interior ministry, with drones and helicopters being used to find victims and remove rubble.
Witnesses described seeing people crying and bleeding, passengers trapped in their seats and smoke billowing throughout the carriages, one of which caught fire.
Sánchez said it was "unacceptable" that Spain had suffered two serious rail disasters this year, after a high-speed crash killed 46 people near Córdoba in January. It occurred on the same line as Wednesday's accident, but much further south.
Most political parties suspended campaigning for upcoming elections following the incident.
The exception was the far-right party Vox. Its leader, Santiago Abascal, said his party would not take part in what he described as attempts to "use mourning to silence criticism" of the country's rail infrastructure.

  - Published12 hours ago
- What we know so far about deadly Spain train crash 
  - Published1 hour ago
- Watch: At the scene of Spain's deadly train crash 
  - Published16 hours ago
Overnight, around 1,500 people gathered outside the Spanish Transport Ministry building in the capital, according to Spanish broadcaster TVE, which reported that demonstrators were largely calling for the resignations of Sánchez and Puente.
Police used tear gas to disperse crowds after protesters hurled bottles and flares. No injuries or arrests were reported.
Rail drivers are expected to go ahead with a planned strike on Thursday, with the Spanish Union of Railway Drivers (Semaf) saying the strike action will be held "in defence of railway safety".
The leader of Spain's main opposition People's Party Alberto Núñez Feijóo said: "Spain has the right to know what is happening with its infrastructure."
Late on Wednesday, relatives were still trying to gather information about passengers who were on either of the trains.
The Spanish Civil Guard has set up bureaus in Madrid, Toledo, Seville and Córdoba to investigate reports of missing persons.
"The top priority is the identification of the missing persons and the taking of DNA samples to be able to locate their relatives," the civil guard wrote in a post on X.
In Toledo, close to the site of the crash, locals observed a minute's silence during a vigil to commemorate the victims.
European Union flags are flying at half-mast in Brussels, in what the European Commission called a "sign of European solidarity" during Spain's mourning period.
Wednesday's crash is the worst the country has seen since 2013, when 80 people died on the outskirts of Santiago de Compostela in north-west Spain.

Official results of Alberta referendum released
Turnout for separation question 10 percentage points higher than the last provincial election
Alberta's referendum question on separation drew more interest from voters than the province's last general election, according to the official results released Thursday.
The final tally of the referendum ballots has been released, 10 days after the vote was held.
More than 2.2 million ballots were cast for the separation question, representing a 70.4 per cent voter turnout — nearly 10 percentage points higher than for the 2023 provincial election.
Albertans soundly rejected the proposal to hold a second, binding referendum on separation, with 74.9 per cent voting against, while narrowly passing the five immigration questions and voting down the four constitutional questions.
A total of 22.1 million votes were cast across the 10 questions, including declined and rejected ballots. The turnout on all questions was around 70 per cent. (Voters could choose which questions they wanted to vote on.)
Question 5, on requiring proof of citizenship to vote in provincial elections, had the highest voter turnout of any question on the ballot. Nearly 600 more people filled out a ballot on that question versus the one on separation.
- Smith scores slim majority on immigration questions, Albertans reject constitutional changes
- Analysis Nopes to the nine? Blue walls? Five takeaways from Alberta's referendum results
The turnout for the other nine questions came as a surprise to Mount Royal University political scientist Lori Williams.
"I think there was a sense that maybe there might be a big gap between the separation question participation rate and the responses on the other nine questions," Williams said.
"Even though those questions were complex, those who did show up and didn't leave the lineup, who went through the trouble to actually do the mail-in or the advance polls or the referendum day voting, almost all of them went through those questions."
But with that high turnout came slim majorities for the five questions that passed.
The immigration questions passed with between 51.7 and 58 per cent support. Williams says those results are "not a really strong mandate" for Premier Danielle Smith.
"It didn't give the government the authority to sort of take the fight to Ottawa in the way that they had hoped to do," Williams said.
Mount Royal University political scientist Lori Williams on Oct. 29, 2026. (Chelsey Mutter/CBC)
The remaining four questions on constitutional reform failed, with between 42.4 and 47.2 per cent voting in favour.
Williams said internal polling and focus groups had led the province to expect a much higher success rate on the questions, and the province "might be more reluctant to go forward with a referendum" in the future since the results turned out so differently than expected.
"That's got to be a bit of a cautionary note," she said.
- Edmonton and Calgary rejected her referendum. Does Danielle Smith have a city problem?
- Alberta pursuing own dental, drug plans despite referendum defeat on federal opt-outs
Elections Alberta to review how referendum went
The official numbers vary by less than a percentage point from the unofficial results available since Sunday.
Counting all of those ballots by hand took about five days, with unofficial results finalized well beyond the 48-hour deadline set out in Alberta's referendum legislation.
An Elections Alberta spokesperson told CBC News the provincial agency is not yet ready to discuss lessons learned from the tumultuous process, and that it "will be conducting reviews, debriefs, data analysis, and data entry" over the next few months.

The agency said the referendum had the highest number of ballots to count by hand in any Canadian electoral event, to its knowledge.

The story so far:
France reported the first known human infection with Shamonda virus on October 22, 2026. The patient, who was severely immunocompromised and receiving treatment for a serious illness at the Hospices Civils de Lyon, died in early October. Investigations are underway to determine whether the virus caused or contributed to the death, and how the patient acquired the infection.
French authorities suspect that the patient was infected by the bite of a Culicoides midge in eastern France, where the virus had been circulating among animals during spring and summer. The specific insect responsible has not been identified. According to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), the virus has been detected in farm animals in Austria, Belgium, France, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Portugal, Spain and Switzerland, as well as Jersey.
French authorities say that no public health risk to the general population has been identified based on current knowledge of the virus. The World Health Organization (WHO) has also said that wider spread is unlikely based on the information currently available. However, investigations into the human case are continuing.
What is Shamonda virus?
Shamonda virus is a vector-borne virus belonging to the genus Orthobunyavirus in the family Peribunyaviridae. It is part of the Simbu group of viruses, which also includes Schmallenberg virus and Akabane virus.
The virus was first isolated from cattle in Nigeria in the mid-1960s and has since been reported sporadically in cattle in parts of Africa and Japan. Before the recent case in France, it was considered an animal pathogen that did not infect humans.
Cattle are considered its main animal hosts, although infections have also been detected in sheep, goats, horses and alpacas. In livestock, infection can cause fever, diarrhoea, lethargy, loss of appetite and reduced milk production. In pregnant animals, it has been associated with abortions and congenital abnormalities in offspring.
Neurological signs have also been reported in horses infected with the virus in Europe. The extent to which the variants circulating in Europe differ in their effects on animal health remains under investigation.
How does it spread?
The virus is understood to spread primarily through the bites of infected Culicoides midges, tiny blood-feeding insects. The precise midge species responsible for transmitting the European variants has not yet been established.
According to the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), there is currently no evidence of horizontal transmission, or spread between animals through direct contact or other routes. Vertical transmission, from a pregnant animal to its offspring, has been reported.
Two genetically distinct variants, designated Shamonda virus Europe 1 (SHAV-EU1) and Shamonda virus Europe 2 (SHAV-EU2), have been identified in Europe in 2026. Research indicates that they may have been introduced separately. Their geographical distribution, effects on livestock and long-term significance remain under investigation.
Why is it in the news?
The detection in a human has raised questions about whether Shamonda virus can cause disease beyond its known animal hosts. French authorities have reported that the brain complications observed in the patient before death were considered very likely to be linked to the infection. However, investigations are continuing to establish whether the virus caused or contributed to the death.
The patient was severely immunocompromised and had an underlying serious illness. It is not yet known whether similar complications would occur in people with different health conditions or whether people without immune suppression could develop symptomatic infection.
The case highlights the importance of the One Health approach, which recognises the links between human, animal and environmental health. Monitoring infections in livestock, investigating unusual human infections and sharing laboratory findings can help identify emerging health risks.
The virus is also affecting livestock production. A study of nine French dairy herds found a 15%–75% decline in bulk milk production during clinical episodes associated with infection. Affected cattle also showed symptoms such as diarrhoea, reduced activity and, less consistently, fever. The findings are from a small number of farms and do not establish the typical impact across all affected herds.
How prevalent is it?
The prevalence of Shamonda virus in humans is unknown. The French case is the first documented human infection, but it does not establish when the virus first began infecting people or whether other infections have gone undetected. There is insufficient data to estimate the number of human infections worldwide.
In animals, the virus has been identified in parts of Africa and Japan. Its detection in European livestock in 2026 has expanded its known geographical distribution. By October 22, the ECDC had reported detections in farm animals across 12 European countries and Jersey.
These reports indicate the geographical spread of detections, not the proportion of animals infected. Differences in veterinary surveillance, laboratory testing and reporting make it difficult to compare the burden between countries.
There are no verified figures establishing the prevalence of Shamonda virus in India so far. However, the absence of reported detections does not establish that the virus is absent from the country.
The virus is not subject to routine official surveillance or control measures under the European Union’s Animal Health Law. This may limit the completeness of information on its distribution and prevalence in livestock.
How is it diagnosed and treated?
In animals, the symptoms of Shamonda virus infection can resemble those of other livestock diseases. Laboratory testing is therefore needed to confirm infection. Molecular tests, including polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays, can detect the virus’s genetic material, while genetic sequencing can help distinguish between variants.
Evidence on the clinical presentation and management of human infection remains limited. There is currently no established, Shamonda-specific treatment protocol for human infection. Further investigation is needed to determine how the virus affects humans and what clinical management may be appropriate.
According to WOAH, there are no commercially available vaccines against Shamonda virus. No established vaccine is available for preventing human infection.
What is the public health risk?
French authorities have said that no public health risk to the general population has been identified based on current knowledge. The WHO has assessed wider spread as unlikely on the available evidence. These assessments reflect what is currently known and may change as further information becomes available.
Key questions include how the patient acquired the infection, whether the virus contributed to the death, whether other human infections have occurred and whether the virus can spread between people. There is currently no evidence of sustained human-to-human transmission.
Surveillance of livestock, laboratory investigations and coordination between animal and human health authorities will be important in answering these questions.
For now, the available evidence supports continued monitoring and investigation. The first human case is significant because the virus was previously considered unable to infect humans, but it does not establish that Shamonda virus is spreading widely among people or that a human outbreak is under way.

Bengaluru’s literary scene is largely kept alive by its legendary bookstores dotting Church Street. From author visits and book signings, to rare books and signed editions, Blossom Book House, Bookworm, Book Hive and a few others in the vicinity have seemingly gained a reputation as Bengaluru’s only literary spaces. While the significance of Church Street cannot be dismissed, readers in other parts of the city have found their favourite nooks. We take a look at bookstores beyond Church Street...
Turning Pages, Jakkur
A two-storey space that includes a café on the ground floor, Turning Pages in Jakkur, houses a collection of books that caters to every reader’s taste. Founded by Vineetha Vijaykumar, it has shelves dedicated to books in regional languages as well as a space for events and community gatherings. Within the bookstore is a roundtable reading space for visitors. “The reason I started Turning Pages is because I enjoy places like this, and it has become increasingly difficult to find them,” Vineetha says. “The idea was to find a space that allowed one to slow down and build human connections, and regain an essence of community.” And Turning Pages does just that, with its welcoming ambience and warmth.
Kadhaigal Bookstore, Sahakar Nagar
Nestled within one of Sahakar Nagar’s quiet neighbourhoods is Kadhaigal Bookstore, a cosy space with a personally curated collection of books for sale, a free library section for children, and a separate shelf for second-hand books. Its founders Ramon and Lakshmi Selvakumaran want to ensure children’s books are easily available in-house for little ones from all backgrounds. Having lived in the neighbourhood for a long time now, their intention to start a bookstore in Sahakar Nagar stemmed from their deep-rooted love for their community.
“Right now, we see readers from a particular bracket in society, but our goal is to be inclusive to people from all backgrounds,” says Ramon. To bring this into effect, Kadhaigal Bookstore has designed events for children and adults such as nature walks and workshops, hoping to build a close-knit community. He hopes to house a larger collection of books and to be able to welcome as many readers as possible. “We don’t want a chain of bookstores across the city or the country; our intent is to build a supportive community here in Sahakar Nagar,” he says.
Dragonfly Reads in Jinvara, Yelahanka
Located in a beautiful community complex, Dragonfly Reads is an all-things-literary store, at Jinvara in Yelahanka. As the official bookstore partner of Himalayan Writing Retreat’s Laidback Lit Fest, this bookstore also caters to a wider online community. Established in February 2024, Dragonfly has been hosting readers from across the city for over two years. From having authors in various fields to monthly book clubs meets, Dragonfly Reads offers an all-round space for readers and artistes to connect and form an intimate community in North Bengaluru.
Paperback Bookshop, Kammanahalli
A tiny bookstore with a curated collection, Paperback Bookshop is the go-to place for quick purchases or to peruse a personalised curation of books. Originally founded in Mumbai by journalists B Mahesh and Usman Merchant, this bookstore boasts two locations in Bengaluru. Their shop in Kammanahalli is a street store with a good range of books housed in an intimate space, while their second store is a part of Ranga Shankara in JP Nagar. When asked about the growing online market, Mahesh says, “I won’t say people should buy books from my store alone; buy books from any place and support physical bookstores.”
Some of the other notable bookstores and community spaces in the city include Champaca in Vasant Nagar and Indiranagar’s Atta Galatta which partners with the annual Bangalore Literature Festival and Bengaluru Poetry Festival.

Delhi traders flag parking, traffic concerns; urge Sonia Gandhi to defer Rahul's rally
NEW DELHI: The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) in Delhi on Friday urged senior Congress leader Sonia Gandhi to postpone the party's proposed mega rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1, warning that it could disrupt business worth Rs 10,000-12,000 crore across 20 markets in the national capital.The trade body said the rally, proposed by leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, comes at a crucial time when markets are preparing for the Diwali shopping season.The trade body warned of severe economic losses during the peak festive shopping season.The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) said the rally is expected to draw around 10 lakh people and 15,000 to 20,000 vehicles to central Delhi. It warned that the large gathering could lead to severe traffic congestion and affect the movement of goods and shoppers across the markets."We demand to reschedule the mega-rally of 1 million (10 lakh) people, planned for November 1, to a date after Diwali; lack of parking for 15,000–20,000 vehicles could lead to a total gridlock, akin to a lockdown," the CTI urged in its letter to Sonia Gandhi.The traders' body said the rally is planned at a crucial time for businesses, with Dhanteras falling on November 6 and Diwali on November 8. It said November 1 is expected to be one of the busiest days for transporting festive goods and for shoppers visiting the markets.
CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said traders were worried about the possible impact on their livelihoods and stressed that the appeal was not against the rally."We are not opposing the rally; we are making a heartfelt plea to protect our livelihoods during the peak Diwali season," stated CTI Chairman Brijesh Goyal."These 20 markets are not merely marketplaces; they are the heartbeat of Delhi. They generate a daily turnover of 10,000 to 12,000 crore rupees, and Dhanteras falls on November 6th. Traders are anxious: if a lockdown-like gridlock hits central Delhi on October 31st and November 1st, how will the goods for Dhanteras be transported in and out?" Goyal added."Dhanteras falls on November 6, and Diwali is on November 8; November 1 is the busiest day for preparations... If 1 million people and 15,000–20,000 vehicles arrive in Central Delhi on November 1, the daily business turnover of Rs 10,000–12,000 crore across 20 historic markets will come to a complete standstill," Goyal noted.
Parking and traffic concerns
In its letter, the CTI listed four major concerns. The first was the lack of parking space at Ramlila Maidan."Where will 15,000–20,000 vehicles be parked? Ramlila Maidan does not even have the capacity to park 200 large buses."The second concern was the possible disruption to 20 wholesale and retail markets within a 5-km radius of the venue. The CTI said these markets together record daily business worth Rs 10,000-12,000 crore.The markets include Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazar, Connaught Place, Palika Bazar, Janpath, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Kashmiri Gate, Naya Bazar, Lajpat Rai Market, Chawri Bazar, Kinari Bazar, Dariba Kalan, Ballimaran, Fatehpuri, Tilak Bazar, Karol Bagh, Jama Masjid, Nabi Karim, Gaffar Market, Ajmeri Gate-Paharganj and Daryaganj.The traders' body also warned that traffic restrictions could begin well before the rally. It said buses and other vehicles may start arriving at Delhi's borders, including Singhu, Tikri, Ghazipur and Badarpur, from the afternoon of October 31. Barricades could also be put up along Bahadur Shah Zafar Marg and JLN Marg by the evening.The CTI said transporters had already begun refusing to send vehicles to the markets from October 31.It also cited the traffic disruption during an earlier protest as a reason for concern."On October 10th, with only 5,000 to 7,000 people gathering at Jantar Mantar, central Delhi remained gridlocked for eight hours. Now, 1 million (10 lakh) people are expected to arrive."The CTI said the markets, some of which are up to 300 years old, supply goods to different parts of the country. It added that their operations depend on around 5,000 trucks and tempos arriving daily from 56 industrial areas, including Narela, Bawana, Okhla, Mayapuri, Mundka, Udyog Nagar and Mangolpuri.
CTI suggests two alternatives
To avoid disruption during the festive season, the CTI has suggested two options. It has asked the organisers to postpone the rally until after November 10 or shift it to Burari Maidan if the November 1 date cannot be changed.
The rally, called the 'Chalo Dilli Ramlila March', has been organised by the opposition INDIA bloc to protest against alleged vote tampering.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has said the march is not limited to any one political party and has appealed to people to join it."Chalo Dilli Ramlila March, it is a march to save democracy, to stop vote theft, to save the Constitution. This is not a march of any one political party; it is a march of the soul of India. All the people who are fed up with Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, and Gyanesh Kumar, all the people who want to save democracy, who want to protect the Constitution, you all come," Rahul Gandhi stated.The letter to Sonia Gandhi came after the trade body had also written to Rahul Gandhi, urging him to postpone the rally to avoid disrupting business during the festive season.With less than 48 hours left before the rally, traders are waiting for a response from the Congress leadership to their request.

The Hindu Group, in association with the Cancer Institute (WIA), Adyar, launched Cancer 360: Overview of Detection, Treatment, Palliation, a book examining cancer care from prevention and early detection to treatment, rehabilitation and palliative care. The book was launched at The Hindu office in Chennai.
N. Ram, director of The Hindu Group, launched the book alongside Suresh Nambath, editor of The Hindu. Mr. Ram handed over the first copy to E. Hemanth Raj, executive vice-chairman of Cancer Institute.
Speaking at the launch, Mr. Ram emphasised the importance of making advanced cancer care accessible and affordable. He highlighted the institute’s work in providing treatment to those who need it most and stressed the need to ensure that advances in cancer care reach patients facing barriers to treatment.
Dr. Hemanth Raj spoke about the need to translate advances in cancer research, much of which takes place in the West, into practical interventions in local settings. He also highlighted the institute’s charitable programmes, supported by donations, to help patients access treatment and facilities, and its plans to expand cancer care to reach more patients.
Arvind Krishnamurthy, professor of surgical oncology at Cancer Institute, stressed the need for continued research to improve cancer care and develop better treatments.
The book also addresses care beyond treatment. Mahalakshmi Rangabashyam Shetty, ENT surgeon and lecturer in the Department of Surgical Oncology at the institute, spoke about individualised treatment plans developed through multidisciplinary consultations. She also highlighted the need to tailor exercise and nutrition regimens to individual patients, alongside supportive services such as hospice care.
Surendran Veeraiah, professor and head of the Department of Regional Cancer Centre (RCTC), Cancer Institute, emphasised the importance of psychological support and allied services. He said the book could help make technical information on comprehensive cancer care accessible to more people.
The book features contributions from experts across oncology and allied disciplines. Its chapters cover multidisciplinary tumour boards, psychological care, onco-physiotherapy, palliative care, cancer research, speech and swallowing rehabilitation, early detection, precision treatment, pathology, nutrition and healthcare quality.
The book is available free of cost to The Hindu subscribers at https://www.thehindu.com/premium/ebook/

In late October, about a week before Election Day, some people on Facebook shared what appeared to be a screenshot of an Oct. 26 Truth Social post by U.S. President Donald Trump in which he preemptively declared victory for every Republican candidate across the country in the midterm elections.
According to the image (archived), the post began:
Why are we wasting time counting ballots? Everybody already knows the Republicans WON the 2026 midterms in a historic landslide! ALL 50 STATES!
I am officially declaring victory for EVERY Republican candidate right now. Every Senate seat, every House seat, every governor's race. The Democrats can count all they want, but it won't change the fact that we won.
(Facebook page Branson Area Breaking News)
Other Facebook accounts shared the image as well, particularly in Facebook Groups (archived). A number of Snopes readers emailed us asking if the screenshot was real.
It was fake. The screenshot was fabricated from whole cloth by Branson Area Breaking News, a Facebook page that labels its content as satirical. Because it was later shared widely without a satire label, we've rate the claim as originated as satire.
A search for the Truth Social post on Trump's Truth (archived), an online archive of Trump's Truth Social posts inclusive of deleted posts, revealed that Trump has never posted about anyone "wasting time counting ballots." The only post in which Trump used the word "midterms" on Oct. 26, 2026, was one offering a reward for anyone reporting voter fraud in the midterms or past elections, according to the archive.
Searches for "Donald Trump wasting time counting ballots" on Google (archived), DuckDuckGo (archived) and Bing (archived) similarly did not reveal any credible news reports on the rumored post. Had the president actually suggested counting ballots was a waste of time and that he was declaring victory for every Republican prior to Election Day, it would have been reported on by national, international and politics-oriented news organizations.
Trump's profile picture in the fabricated screenshot differs from the profile picture he actually uses on Truth Social. The profile picture in the screenshot depicts fewer stars on the left side of his face than the real one. Trump's face in the fabricated profile picture is also rounder than his in the actual profile picture.
That the screenshot was fake shouldn't be too surprising for readers familiar with Branson Area Breaking News. The Facebook page's bio (archived) says, "We are a world renowned satirical news organization & have received many awards for our breaking news stories! ***All content on our page is original.***" The page's label reads "satire/parody."
Branson Area Breaking News usually features Branson, Missouri, in its satirical posts. All 12 of Snopes' previous 12 fact-checks regarding Branson, Missouri, were rumors originating from the page, which frequently uses artificial intelligence tools to create the content it posts.
Let us note here: Whether you agree with something being described as satire or parody is a matter of opinion. Snopes is in the business of facts. We label these rumors based on creators' description of them. Your call on whether you agree.

SURAT: A US court has ordered a Virginia resident to remove his encroachment from land owned by the late Kanu Gandhi, Mahatma Gandhi’s grandson, and his wife Shiva Gandhi, after a 20-month legal battle led by Parimal Desai from Surat.
The dispute involved 30 acres of land adjoining Shenandoah National Park in Warren County, Virginia, which the Gandhi couple bought in 1987. During their final years in South Gujarat, they created a charitable trust and transferred their assets to it. Desai now serves as managing trustee.
Talking to TOI, Parimal Desai said, “It began when US national Gregory Black sent a legal notice to my residence on Jan 10, 2025. Black claimed the land by the adverse possession rule of Virginia, which allows a person to own land after 15 years of possession if five conditions are met. He ultimately could not prove his exclusive and actual possession condition and the ‘hostile claim’ condition.”
Kanu Gandhi and Shiva Gandhi returned to India in 2013 and spent their final years in South Gujarat. Kanu Gandhi died in Surat in Nov 2016. Under his will, his assets passed to Shiva Gandhi.
In 2018, Shiva Gandhi established ‘The Dr Schiva and Kanu Ramdas Mohandas Gandhi Charitable Trust’ and registered her will. After her death in 2020, the will was executed and Desai took charge as managing trustee. The trust inherited her properties and financial assets to support its charitable activities.
Desai said he first visited the Virginia property in 2024 and commissioned a survey at a cost of $4,500.
“As I learnt about the land in Virginia, I went to the property in 2024 and got the survey done. If the trust wanted to do anything with land, it had to be in its possession. I got the will probated in a US court in 2025 and got the land title in the trust’s name,” he said.
Black claimed he had occupied the land since 2008. In court he cited trails, a cabin, tree stands, a culvert and other improvements on the property, along with photographs from to support his claim.
Desai said, “I had hired lawyers in the US and worked in India to win the claim. I used artificial intelligence (AI) to find the ways to contest the claim. When the final trial took place, from Sep 8 to 11, I told the court that Kanu Gandhi was Mahatma Gandhi’s grandson and he and his wife has donated the properties to the trust, which has the objective of propagating Gandhian philosophy.
“We could prove with GIS maps that the cabin was not there for 15 years. I also went there many times since 2020 which disproved his claim of actual possession. We also found another woman residing on the land, which belied Black’s claim that he had exclusive possession.”
In the order dated Oct 21, Judge Daryl L. Funk of the Warren County Circuit Court ruled in favour of Desai and the trust. The court directed Black to pay $11,375 towards the fees of the Guardian ad Litem representing unknown heirs.
The court also ordered Black to remove the cabin, hunting stands, hunting huts and personal belongings from the property within 30 days at his own expense. Black was directed to surrender possession of the land and cease entering or exercising any ownership rights over it.

The revised Maximum Retail Price (MRP) list of anti-cancer medicines published by the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) raises serious concerns about excessive pricing and the exploitation of patients, noted medical health activists on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).
Editorial | Bitter pills: on Court’s intervention, drug pricing
The NPPA, under the Department of Pharmaceuticals, Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers, has released a list of 543 brands of anti-cancer medicines with their revised MRP that will be effective from November 9.
“The revised price list reflects the information submitted by companies up to October 27, 2026, and it will be updated as and when manufacturers submit their revised prices of non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs,” said a release issued by the Union government on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).
On October 17, the NPPA had announced Trade Margin Rationalisation (TMR) of 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs in public interest to address excessive trade margins, make cancer treatment more affordable, and improve access to anti-cancer medicines. Manufacturers were instructed to submit their revised list to NPPA.
The 137 non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs include immunotherapy medicines used in the treatment of over 20 types of cancer, Denosumab used by breast and prostate cancer patients, Pegfilgrastim used to prevent neutropenia in cancer patients, and Bevacizumab, which is approved for the treatment of colon, ovarian and cervical cancers.
Curbing profiteering
Stating that cost-based price control can further reduce medicine prices and curb excessive profiteering, Jan Swasthya Abhiyan India (JSA India), an organisation working for accessibility of medicines, said that controlling trade margins alone is insufficient. Life-saving cancer treatment must be affordable based on medical need, not a patient’s ability to pay.
In their statement, the group explained: “For example, the reported MRP of one brand of palbociclib fell from approximately ₹40,421 to ₹2,720 per pack, while thiotepa fell from approximately ₹80,072 to ₹7,150 per vial. Such drastic reductions raise serious questions about the pricing practices of pharmaceutical companies, including major Indian manufacturers of generic cancer medicines that have reportedly offered substantial trade margins while patients continued to face unaffordable prices.’’
It added that, several patented cancer medicines remain exorbitantly priced. The Trade Margin Rationalisation (TMR) policy has failed to ensure affordability, while excluding medicines supplied free under Patient Assistance Programmes from its calculations has further limited its potential impact on patients, said the group.
“The policy’s formula is also deeply flawed. Allowing a 42.8% markup over the Price to Stockist [PTS] legitimises excessive margins, particularly in a supply chain often involving only one or two intermediaries or direct sales to hospitals. A substantially lower markup, comparable to the 16% margin applicable to scheduled formulations under the DPCO framework, could have delivered greater benefits to patients. A one-time MRP reduction is not enough. Without permanent, enforceable margin caps, regular monitoring and verification by NPPA, excessive pricing can persist or re-emerge,” JSA stated in the release.
The NPPA must also strengthen its collection and maintenance of price data across supply chains and distribution channels, the group said, adding that companies should not be left to calculate and self-report revised MRPs without adequate independent verification.
Tanvi Singh, medical oncologist, MOC Cancer Care, said that cancer is an ailment whose treatment demands are extensive so when drug costs are high, patients may end up delaying treatment initiation, or skipping doses, or even discontinue therapy prematurely. All of these will in turn affect and compromise outcomes.
“Lowering drug costs is an imperative that can improve treatment continuity, reduce financial toxicity, and help patients complete the prescribed course of therapy. However, price caps are not enough on their own. Meaningful and sufficient improvement in affordability can be said to be achieved when price regulation is complemented by wider insurance coverage expansion of government reimbursement schemes, increased availability of quality generic and biosimilar medicines, robust Patient Assistance Programmes (PAPs), and greater access to comprehensive cancer care across the country,” said Dr. Singh.
Sandeep Nayak, chairman of oncology, MACS-Renova Oncology Institute, KIMS Hospital, Bengaluru, said: “The price control introduced by the government is a positive move. But low cost life-saving drugs should remain viable to manufacture and seller.”

For nearly a quarter of a century, Elon Musk and his essential partner at SpaceX, Gwynne Shotwell, viewed the United States government as El Dorado, the mythical city of gold.
Like machete-wielding treasure hunters, Musk and Shotwell hacked through a tangled jungle filled with lurking carnivores such as Boeing and Lockheed Martin, as well as bean counters and regulators. Over time, against long odds, the pair cleared a path for SpaceX to contracts at NASA and the US military. They sued when things did not go their way. They hollered about unfair playing fields. Most importantly, they delivered quality space products to the US government for less.
And so, after a while, SpaceX found El Dorado and a city of contracts.
Then they started winning everything. So much so that the relationship between the customer and contractor began to change. Slowly at first, but ever more quickly, SpaceX went from needing the US government as an indispensable customer to becoming an indispensable contractor for the nation.
The pendulum has swung so far now that SpaceX seems increasingly disinterested in the US government for most contracts outside of data services, such as Starshield for military communications and observations.
“I guess I am still in denial that there is a divorce pending,” said Lori Garver, a deputy NASA administrator during the Obama White House years who was instrumental in expanding the agency’s use of commercial contracts with companies like SpaceX. “I literally cannot wrap my head around a future yet where SpaceX stops flying Dragon and Falcon. Not yet.”
But the signs point to at least a partial breakup. Consider the following data points:
- SpaceX has told NASA it will stop flying Crew Dragon, the space agency’s only reliable astronaut transportation to the International Space Station, by or before 2030. Shotwell said in September that NASA should rely instead on Boeing for astronaut transportation. “We’re just gonna let them have some business,” she said of Boeing. “They should fly their capsule. The government paid a lot of money for that.” As a result, NASA is investing more in Boeing.
- Ars reported in October that SpaceX had stopped selling commercial launches on the Falcon 9 rocket for missions after the year 2028.
- SpaceX may also still stop flying Falcon 9 for NASA missions. In late October, during a meeting of NASA’s Safety Advisory Panel, Kent Rominger said if the US Deorbit Vehicle (a modified Dragon spacecraft) launches to the International Space Station after 2030, “it may require” a rocket other than the Falcon 9.
- Politico reported last week that SpaceX told the US Space Force it would not bid on three new launch contracts in the late 2020s that would have gone above and beyond its existing commitments to the US military.
- SpaceX previously provided “Rough Order of Magnitude” estimates, or ROMs, for launch costs to US companies building small landers for NASA’s Moon Base as part of the Commercial Lunar Payload Services program. But according to three sources, SpaceX recently told these lunar companies they will not provide launch services.

22 అక్టోబర్ 2026న, అరుణాచల్ ప్రదేశ్ సరిహద్దు వెంబడి పలు ప్రదేశాలలో భారత సైనికులకు చైనా బలగాలతో ఘర్షణలు జరిగాయని ఇండో-టిబెటన్ బోర్డర్ పోలీస్ (ITBP) డైరెక్టర్ జనరల్ శత్రుజీత్ కపూర్ అంగీకరించారు. చైనా సైనికులు నిర్ధారిత గస్తీ పద్ధతులను పాటించనప్పుడు వాస్తవ నియంత్రణ రేఖ (LAC) వెంబడి పరిస్థితి “అస్తవ్యస్తంగా” మారుతుందని విదేశీ వ్యవహారాల మంత్రిత్వ శాఖ (MEA) ప్రతినిధి రణధీర్ జైస్వాల్ మరుసటిరోజు పేర్కొన్నారు.
ఈ నేపథ్యంలో భారత్, చైనా సైనికుల మధ్య ఘర్షణలకు సంబంధించిన దృశ్యాలంటూ కొన్ని వీడియోలు (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) సోషల్ మీడియాలో ప్రచారంలో ఉన్నాయి. వీటిలో ఎంత నిజముందో ఇప్పుడు చూద్దాం.
క్లెయిమ్: అక్టోబర్ 2026లో అరుణాచల్ ప్రదేశ్ సరిహద్దు (LAC) వద్ద భారత, చైనా సైనికుల మధ్య జరిగిన ఘర్షణలకు సంబంధించిన దృశ్యాలు.
ఫాక్ట్: ఈ వైరల్ వీడియోలన్నీ పాతవి లేదా అక్టోబర్ 2026 నాటి ఘర్షణలకు సంబంధం లేనివి. ఇవి 2021, 2024, 2025 సంవత్సరాలకు చెందిన పాత ఘటనలు, జూలై 2026 నాటి అమర్నాథ్ యాత్రకు సంబంధించిన దృశ్యాలు. కావున, ఈ వీడియోలు తప్పుదోవ పట్టించే విధంగా ఉన్నాయి.
వీడియో 1
ఈ వీడియో కనీసం డిసెంబర్ 2022 నుండే ఇంటర్నెట్లో ఉన్నట్లు గుర్తించాం. అంటే, ఈ వీడియో అక్టోబర్ 2026లో రిపోర్ట్ చేయబడిన భారత్-చైనా సరిహద్దు ఉద్రిక్తతల కంటే ముందే ఉందని, తాజా పరిణామాలతో దీనికి సంబంధం లేదని స్పష్టమవుతుంది. డిసెంబర్ 2022లో ప్రచురితమైన ఒక CNN కథనంలో, ఇదే దృశ్యాలను చూపిస్తూ, ఈ వీడియో సెప్టెంబర్ 2021లో చిత్రీకరించినట్లు పేర్కొన్నారు. ఈ వీడియో వాస్తవ నియంత్రణ రేఖ సమీపంలో అరుణాచల్ ప్రదేశ్లో చిత్రీకరించినట్లుగా భారతీయ సైనకాధికారి ధృవీకరించారని ఈ కథనం పేర్కొంది.
వీడియో 2
వైరల్ వీడియోలోని దృశ్యాలు రివర్స్ ఇమేజ్ సెర్చ్ చేయగా, ఇదే వీడియో కనీసం నవంబర్ 2024 (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) నుంచి ఇంటర్నెట్లో ఉన్నట్లు గుర్తించాం. అరుణాచల్ ప్రదేశ్లోకి చొరబడటానికి ప్రయత్నిస్తున్న చైనా సైనికులను భారత సైనికులు అడ్డుకుని దాడి చెయ్యడం ఈ వీడియో చూపుతుందని ఆ పోస్టులు పేర్కొన్నాయి. ఇండియన్ ఆర్మీ ఫ్యాక్ట్-చెక్ విభాగం కూడా ఈ వీడియోను ఖండిస్తూ ‘X’లో చేసిన పోస్ట్ చేసింది.
వీడియో 3
ఈ వీడియోకి సంబంధించిన దృశ్యాలు కనీసం జూలై 2026 నుంచి ఇంటర్నెట్లో అందుబాటులో ఉన్నట్లు గుర్తించాం. వీటి ప్రకారం, అమర్నాథ్ యాత్ర 2026 సందర్భంగా, జమ్మూ & కాశ్మీర్లోని బాల్తాల్ వద్ద ప్రవేశ ద్వారం దగ్గర యాత్రికులు నమోదు చేసుకోవడానికి, RFID కార్డులను పొందడానికి గుమిగూడిన దృశ్యాలను ఈ వీడియో చూపుతుంది. ఇండియన్ ఆర్మీ ఫ్యాక్ట్-చెక్ విభాగం కూడా ఈ వీడియోను ఖండిస్తూ ‘X’లో చేసిన పోస్ట్ చేసింది.
వీడియో 4
మా దర్యాప్తులో డిసెంబర్ 2025 నాటి అవే దృశ్యాలతో కూడిన అనేక సోషల్ మీడియా పోస్టులను (ఇక్కడ, ఇక్కడ & ఇక్కడ) గుర్తించాం. ఈ పోస్టుల ప్రకారం, ఆరోగ్య సమస్యలతో బాధపడుతున్న ఒక భారతీయ సైనికుడు వాస్తవ నియంత్రణ రేఖ (LAC) సమీపంలో విధి నిర్వహణలో ఉండగా స్పృహ కోల్పోయాడు. మీడియా కథనాల ప్రకారం, చైనా పీపుల్స్ లిబరేషన్ ఆర్మీ (PLA) సిబ్బంది అతనికి ప్రథమ చికిత్స, వైద్య సహాయం అందించిన తర్వాత, అతని సొంత యూనిట్కు అప్పగించారు.
చివరిగా, అరుణాచల్ ప్రదేశ్లో 2026 అక్టోబర్లో జరిగిన భారత-చైనా ఘర్షణల దృశ్యాలంటూ సంబంధంలేని పాత వీడియోలను షేర్ చేస్తున్నారు.

Trump's increasing support for Russia carries existential danger for Canada
Carney welcomes EU as experts warn of burgeoning Russian-American alliance
In the six weeks between Prime Minister Mark Carney's trip to the European Parliament and top EU officials arriving for a joint summit in Montreal, the United States has moved considerably closer to Russia.
Just days after Carney returned to Canada, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio invited Russia's Vladimir Putin to December's G20 summit in Miami. Then on Oct. 9, the U.S. lifted sanctions on Russian oil and announced a deal to buy diesel directly from Russia.
Some analysts say Trump's rapprochement with Russia poses a clear danger to Canadians — one not easily solved by closer partnerships with allies an ocean away.
"This is not Trump playing footsie with Putin," said Vincent Rigby, national security and intelligence adviser to the prime minister until 2021. "This is something far, far more serious, and strategically, this can't help but be a concern."
Last week on the White House South Lawn, Trump drew his own parallels between Canada and Ukraine, bragging after a call with Carney: "Just like I told Zelenskyy, we have all the cards."
While Trump has increased his swipes at Canada on the campaign trail, his hostility to Ukraine goes beyond words.
In Trump's one-sided "energy ceasefire," Ukraine was expected to stop hitting Russian refineries but Russia continued to hit Ukrainian electrical plants.
Then came the slowdown in Starlink/Starshield, followed by a round of blame-shifting between the White House and Elon Musk as to who ordered it. The U.S. also appeared to cut off warnings of incoming ballistic missiles, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Trump is making it harder to access Patriot missiles.
"It's been unbelievable," said Rob Huebert, director of the Centre for Military, Security and Strategic Studies at the University of Calgary. "These actions can only be characterized as Trump trying to cause Ukraine to lose the war."
Washington also reportedly leaned on European countries to release billions of Euros in frozen Russian assets, and Trump signed an executive order waiving sanctions against Russia due to take effect two days later.
Maria Popova, an expert on Russia at McGill University and author of Russia and Ukraine: Entangled Histories, Diverging States, says the second Trump administration worked in its first year to make the U.S. more of a neutral party in Russia's war with Ukraine.
She says it now appears Trump is working up to openly allying with Putin.
"We have to start thinking about where this trajectory ends up eventually," she said. "And it ends in the U.S. directly helping Russia's war effort."
Rigby says U.S.-Russian closeness raises immediate fears about Arctic sovereignty, and "could be the end of NORAD in a worst-case scenario," referring to the joint Canada-U.S. partnership to protect sovereign airspace.
Huebert says the lifted oil sanctions and diesel deal could be seen cynically as a temporary move to mollify American voters angry about gas prices.
"For him to try to reduce the price of diesel just before the midterms, you may disagree with it entirely but you can at least understand it," he said.
"But all this other stuff?"
Strongman summit in Shenzhen
A proposed summit between Trump, Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping next month has revived longstanding concerns that Trump is keen to replace America's postwar network of alliances with a new global carve-up between three strongmen.
Trump has expressed openness to the Russian proposal. "Obviously, this is music to Putin's ears," said Popova.
Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said on Sunday that preparations have begun for the three-way summit on the sidelines of the Nov. 18-19 APEC summit in Shenzhen, China.
Huebert says the Russians have long pitched the idea of superpower spheres of influence, in which Washington, Moscow and Beijing would all agree to stay out of each other's backyards. Lesser powers would have to find a modus vivendi with the regional hegemon.
"We really need to be pushing against such a travesty," said Popova, "because the next meeting of the three of them will be to decide the fate of Canada or Taiwan. So we don't want this pattern to even start."
Trump has already made it clear that he sees the entire Western Hemisphere as the domain of the United States.
"We don't want a world that's run by superpowers," said Rigby. "If this is where we're headed — spheres of influence, Russia, China and the United States — this goes back to what Prime Minister Carney said at Davos: that middle powers are effectively going to be marginalized.
"It's very, very concerning."
Living with threats
Canada is pursuing new alliances and rearming, while seeking to keep the U.S.-Canada temperature low and bilateral institutions functioning where possible.
Popova sees parallels in this to Ukraine's past "multi-vector" approach to build connections with other countries, including Canada, that proved invaluable in 2014 when Russia took Crimea.
"In a world that is really becoming a world à trois to a considerable extent, Russia, China, United States, we're going to have to reach out to Europe," said Rigby.
That alliance can strengthen Canadian sovereignty if it leads to deeper integration of defence-industrial bases, greater exchanges of technology, the creation of a payments system less vulnerable to U.S. interference or the launching of new satellites that allow Canadians and Europeans to develop communications and navigational systems that don't depend on Musk or the Pentagon.
But Canada can't alter its geography. It lacks one key advantage of Ukraine, which has land borders with four EU nations, allowing easy resupply. Canada, in the event of real threats or hostilities from the U.S., would be mostly on its own.
Fortunately for Canadians, Trump's hostility toward Canada and fondness for Russia aren't shared by most Americans. For some time, Americans have not trusted Trump to do the right thing on Russia, and that is true also within his own party. Americans, including many Republicans, also don't like Trump's trade war with Canada.
Trump is also unlikely to be as long-lasting as Putin has been. Unless he's able to subvert the U.S. Constitution, he has only 26 months left.
But Rigby says he expects those months to be tumultuous: "You are potentially going to see a president after next week being even more reckless, less restrained and more aggressive."

How could Israel break election deadlock? Here are four scenarios
- Published
Israel looks to be in political deadlock.
With 85% of votes counted after Tuesday's election, neither the incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's coalition, nor the bloc of his key challenger Gadi Eisenkot look set to have a majority.
In order to form a government, it looks likely one of the leading parties would have to break their campaign promises - meaning the most probable outcome may well be new elections.
Here are four possible scenarios.
National unity government led by Netanyahu
Could Netanyahu persuade Eisenkot to join him in a national unity government?
Eisenkot would have to abandon his key platform to do so. He's framed himself as the only alternative to Netanyahu, and built his campaign on ousting him from power.
Just last night, he took to the stage at his campaign HQ and called on Netanyahu to "announce his retirement from political life today," telling the crowd that Israelis are fed up with Netanyahu's "culture of lies", "division and incitement".
But that was before one of the main exit polls - which had initially projected a lead for Eisenkot's bloc - was revised, and he was overtaken by Netanyahu.
Netanyahu could try to persuade Eisenkot's Yashar Party to join his Likud Party in a unity government by ditching the far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties he is currently in coalition with. But last night at Likud HQ he thanked his "loyal partners" and called for a "strong right-wing government"- remarks some have interpreted as meaning he intends to preserve his alliance with them.
One thing that could make a unity government more likely is a renewed conflict with Iran, which could place serious pressure on party leaders to put aside their political differences and work together. In the days prior to the election, Israeli and US media reported that Netanyahu was pushing for fresh strikes on the country, and had pressed Donald Trump to approve US involvement.
This would no-doubt be framed by Netanyahu's critics as an attempt to save his own political skin by entering another regional conflict.
Eisenkot-led coalition with Arab parties
This would be a seismic shift for Israeli politics. Only one independent Arab party has ever formally been part of a coalition, in 2021, and it didn't last long.
Eisenkot and every other Jewish party in his bloc bar one have already ruled out entering government with them. But right now, it's the opposition's only path to a majority.
The Arab parties were the story of election night. They look to have defied expectations and could gain a record 19 seats - helped by an unprecedented turnout from Israel's Arab population, who account for about one-fifth of the country and often describe themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel.
For years, many boycotted Israeli elections, saying voting would legitimise a system that they say treats them as second-class citizens. But their turnout last night, inspired by a desire to oust the most right-wing governing coalition in Israel's history, has shaken things up.
The United Arab list, who are currently projected to win around 7 seats, have said they'd join an opposition government, while The Joint List, who are projected to win 12 seats, have said they'd support one from outside.
However, the only Jewish leader advocating this scenario right now is The Democrats' Yair Golan. And a coalition like this would be very fragile, especially on issues like Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
The fact there is such a unified front from the Jewish parties against Arab participation points to Israel's deep divisions.
Netanyahu-led majority, with right-wingers from opposition
Could Netanyahu persuade the right-wing parties in Eisenkot's bloc to break away and join his coalition?
The two most likely candidates for this are Naftali Bennett - joint-leader of the Beyachad political alliance - and Avigdor Lieberman, leader of the Yisrael Beiteinu party. They are both right-wingers who are hardline on security, and share some political ground with Netanyahu.
But both campaigned explicitly to oust him, and to extend military conscription to the ultra-Orthodox - bringing them into direct conflict with the two ultra-Orthodox parties already part of Netanyahu's government. So it's difficult to see them joining forces.
Some have suggested Bennett and Lieberman's parties could replace the ultra-Orthodox parties, but current electoral math suggests that grouping may not have the seats needed for a majority.
New elections
If none of the above scenarios can be negotiated, the default outcome would be new elections.
Many would see this as a tacit win for Netanyahu, who would remain as caretaker PM until the new elections take place - which he may believe he has a better chance of winning.
Some analysts think the high Arab turnout would not be replicated again - especially if their record representation in parliament led to no change - and it could also mobilise more right-wing voters in a second poll. Netanyahu may also bet that the estimated 70,000 Israelis who flew home from abroad to vote, and are thought to skew against him, wouldn't do so again.
Additionally, several right-wing parties who failed to pass the electoral threshold of 3.25% may attract fewer votes or may not even run, thereby bringing more votes to Likud and its allies.
Between 2019 and 2022, Israel held five separate elections as Netanyahu and his rivals struggled time and again to co-operate.
